abstract: 5-methylcytosine (5mC) and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) are genome-wide epigenetic modifications involved in chromatin organization and transcriptional regulation. Although Enzymatic Methyl-seq (EM-seq) can enable the combined profiling of 5mC and 5hmC, Enzymatic 5hmC-seq (E5hmC-seq) can provide selective profiling of 5hmC at single-base resolution. In this context, we systematically validated E5hmC-seq using diverse genomic DNA samples. Next, we integrated E5hmC-seq with EM-seq to distinguish between 5mC and 5hmC landscapes during neuronal differentiation of mouse embryonic stem cells. First, we observed dynamic remodeling of both modifications throughout differentiation, with pronounced changes during the transition from embryoid bodies (EBs) to neural progenitor cells (NPCs), characterized by a global decrease in 5hmC accompanied by an increase in 5mC. Subsequently, differentially hydroxymethylated regions (DhMRs) exhibiting 5hmC depletion frequently showed a concurrent increase in 5mC, whereas regions gaining 5hmC displayed an opposing trend, reflecting the genome-wide relationship. Mapping these modifications to transcriptional profiles revealed an association between cytosine modification dynamics and gene expression, where transcriptional downregulation correlated with 5hmC depletion with concomitant 5mC enrichment. In summary, combined mapping of EM-seq and E5hmC-seq can decipher the dynamic interplay between 5mC and 5hmC at single-base resolution and provide insights into the relationships among cytosine modification dynamics, genomic context and transcriptional regulation during differentiation.
